review_notes: I read the whole file and checked Mathlib's Ideal/Maps.lean for existing replacements (comap_map_of_surjective, map_isPrime_of_surjective, map_eq_top_or_isMaximal_of_surjective). I found no Mathlib lemma that gives the contraction of an extended ideal along mk I when I ≤ p in one step, so the shared lemmas below are new. I did not compile the rewrites. π and π₂ are `set` abbreviations for Ideal.Quotient.mk, so the rewrites should go through by defeq, but this is untested. Most of the file shows no other substantial duplication. The exists_isIdempotentElem_notMem_iff lemmas and the Zariski main theorem part are not repeated elsewhere.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out twice. Take an idempotent e outside a prime p. Show span{1-e} ≤ p using e*(1-e)=0 and primality. Show p.map (mk I) is prime. Compute its contraction back to p. Lines 217-229 do this for (S, q, e, I, π). Lines 244-257 do it for (S₁, q₁, ε', J, π₂), in the same order: h1e/h1ε', hIq/hJq₁, hkerπ/hkerπ₂, hq₁p/hq₂p, hcomap₁/hcomap₂. The contraction proof `comap_map_of_surjective … ker_eq_comap_bot … mk_ker … sup_eq_left` appears a third time in the earlier theorem, in hcomap at lines 85-87.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas before the main theorem.

(1) `theorem span_one_sub_le_of_notMem {B : Type*} [CommRing B] {e : B} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (p : Ideal B) [p.IsPrime] (hep : e ∉ p) : Ideal.span ({1 - e} : Set B) ≤ p`. Proof: `rw [Ideal.span_le, Set.singleton_subset_iff]`. Then `have h0 : e * (1 - e) ∈ p := by rw [mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self]; exact p.zero_mem`. Then `exact (‹p.IsPrime›.mem_or_mem h0).resolve_left hep`.

(2) `theorem comap_map_mk_of_le {B : Type*} [CommRing B] {I p : Ideal B} (h : I ≤ p) : (p.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = p`. Proof: `rw [Ideal.comap_map_of_surjective _ Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective, ← RingHom.ker_eq_comap_bot, Ideal.mk_ker, sup_eq_left.mpr h]`.

Rewrite the first use as `have hIq : I ≤ q := span_one_sub_le_of_notMem he q heq`, `haveI hq₁p : q₁.IsPrime := Ideal.map_isPrime_of_surjective hπsurj (by rw [hkerπ]; exact hIq)` and `have hcomap₁ : q₁.comap π = q := comap_map_mk_of_le hIq`. This replaces h1e and the old hIq (lines 217-223) and shortens hcomap₁.

Rewrite the second use as `have hJq₁ : J ≤ q₁ := span_one_sub_le_of_notMem hε' q₁ hε'q₁`, the same `map_isPrime_of_surjective` call, and `have hcomap₂ : q₂.comap π₂ = q₁ := comap_map_mk_of_le hJq₁`. This replaces h1ε' and the old hJq₁ (lines 244-250).

In the first theorem, replace the body of hcomap (lines 85-87) by `comap_map_mk_of_le hle`. This works because `Ideal.Quotient.mk 𝔪A` has the same form. The hypotheses are met: hq (q prime), heq and hε'q₁ give the 'e ∉ p' facts, and the imports are already `Mathlib`.
findings.benefit: The two parallel 12-line blocks, plus a third copy of the contraction proof, become one-line applications of two named lemmas. A reader can see that S₂ is built from S₁ the same way S₁ is built from S. A change to the argument is made once.

findings.problem: hI0 and hJ0 prove the same fact twice. If a ring hom f sends the idempotent e to a unit, then f(1-e)=0. The proof is: e(1-e)=0, so f e * f(1-e)=0, then cancel the unit. This is then extended to the whole principal ideal span{1-e} through `mem_span_singleton'` and `map_mul`. Lines 286-295 do it for algebraMap S Sq and e. Lines 298-311 do it for g₁ and ε'. Only the ring hom, the idempotent and the unit proof differ.
findings.proposed_change:
Add `theorem map_one_sub_eq_zero_of_isUnit {B C : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing C] (f : B →+* C) {e : B} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hu : IsUnit (f e)) : f (1 - e) = 0`. Proof: `have h0 : f e * f (1 - e) = 0 := by rw [← map_mul, mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self, map_zero]`, then `exact hu.mul_right_eq_zero.mp h0`.

Then hI0 becomes: `intro s hs; rw [hIdef] at hs; obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton'.mp hs; rw [map_mul, map_one_sub_eq_zero_of_isUnit (algebraMap S Sq) he (hunitq e heq), mul_zero]`.

hJ0 keeps its lines that build ε₀, hε₀q and hu, and ends with `rw [map_mul, map_one_sub_eq_zero_of_isUnit g₁ hε' hu, mul_zero]`. The deleted lines are the h0/h1 calculations. The hypotheses are those already in scope: he, heq, hε', and the unit facts hunitq e heq and hu.
findings.benefit: The cancellation argument, which carries the idempotent reasoning, is stated and proved once. Each use reduces to checking that f e is a unit, which is the only step specific to that use.

findings.problem: Two proofs show that a proper ideal containing 1-e cannot contain e, each by writing 1 as (1-e)+e and using `eq_top_iff_one`. In htop (lines 146-152) it is done by hand with `ring`. In huniq (lines 266-276) it is done through `π₂ ((1 - ε') + ε')`, `sub_add_cancel` and `map_one`. The argument is the same.
findings.proposed_change:
Add `theorem notMem_of_one_sub_mem {B : Type*} [CommRing B] {e : B} {N : Ideal B} (hN : N ≠ ⊤) (h : 1 - e ∈ N) : e ∉ N`. Proof: `intro he; apply hN; rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]; simpa using N.add_mem h he`.

In htop, replace lines 146-152 by `have hε𝔑 : ε ∉ 𝔑 := notMem_of_one_sub_mem h𝔑.ne_top h1ε`.

In huniq, replace the by_contra block 266-276 by `have hε'𝔐 : ε' ∉ 𝔐.comap π₂ := notMem_of_one_sub_mem hmax.ne_top (by rw [Ideal.mem_comap]; ...)`. The remaining goal is π₂ (1-ε') ∈ 𝔐, which follows from the existing h0 fact π₂ (1-ε') = 0 and zero_mem. Here hmax is the already-proved maximality of 𝔐.comap π₂, so ne_top is available. The ring is commutative, which is all the lemma needs.
findings.benefit: This removes a second hand-rolled copy of the 'cannot contain both e and 1-e' argument. It makes it clear that both places use the same fact about complementary idempotents. This is a weaker finding than the first two because each copy is only about 6 lines.
